message.content:
Implement 4 DATA-SAFETY fixes in /opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts (Nxeon migration engine). Edit only that file. After editing run `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit` until CLEAN (exit 0) and `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsx --test test/migrate-consolidate.test.ts` (stays green). Do NOT run the worker, deploy, or commit. These prevent a migration from silently blanking or clobbering a customer DATABASE while reporting success — get them exactly right and conservative. Report final line numbers + summary per fix.

Read the relevant regions FIRST: the compose bring-up loop (search `plan.composeDirs`, `composeEnvFor`, `ce.fileArg`, `ce.composeFiles`, `-p `, the `stateNow`/running-count verdict), the named-volume copy (search `dockerVolumes`, `/var/lib/docker/volumes`, `rsyncPull` of `_data`), the STANDALONE empty-volume guard (search `_data`, `-mindepth 1 -print -quit`, `postgres|mysql|mariadb|mongo`), the SrcContainer `project` field (~1038/1260, `c.project`), the DB dump/import (search `mysqldump`, `pg_dumpall`, `CREATE DATABASE`, the `mysql <` / `psql` import). Note: an opt-in flag `MIGRATE_RENAME_CLONE_CONTAINERS` and `SRC_READONLY` already exist near line 233 — define the new flag there too.

## FIX F2 — replay the source compose PROJECT NAME (prevents orphaned copied volume → silent empty DB)
Problem: bring-up runs `cd ${dir} && ${composeCmd} … up -d` with NO `-p`, so the project name defaults to the target dir basename. But copied named volumes keep the SOURCE's names (`<sourceProject>_<vol>`). If the source used `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`/`-p`/top-level `name:` so its project ≠ dir basename, compose creates FRESH EMPTY volumes and the copied data is orphaned → DB boots blank, reported "running".
Fix: determine the source project name per dir and pass `-p <project>` on bring-up so volume/network prefixes match the copied data. Source project is available from `srcContainers` — find a container whose compose working-dir/label maps to this dir and read its `com.docker.compose.project` label (`c.project`), keyed the same way `srcComposeFiles` already maps dir→files (grep `srcComposeFiles` — mirror that map to build `srcProjectName: Map<dir,string>`). Also parse a top-level `name:` from the compose file as a fallback. Apply `-p ${proj}` to the `up -d` AND to the verdict's `ps -q`/`config` calls for that project (they must target the same project). If no source project name is known, keep current behavior (dir-basename default) — do not force a `-p` you can't justify. IMPORTANT: the existing clone-rename path (`MIGRATE_RENAME_CLONE_CONTAINERS`) already sets its own `-p <proj>` — make sure F2's `-p` and the clone path don't double-apply; the clone path's explicit `-p` should win for a renamed clone.

## FIX F3 — port the empty-volume refusal to the COMPOSE path (compose has none today)
The STANDALONE path already refuses to start a `(postgres|mysql|mariadb|mongo)` container whose named volume `_data` is empty (search that guard). The COMPOSE path has no equivalent. Add, BEFORE `up -d` for a project: resolve the project's named volumes and their effective target names (using the F2 project prefix), and for any whose image/service is a known stateful engine (postgres/mysql/mariadb/mongo — reuse the same regex the standalone guard uses) AND whose target volume `_data` is empty (`find /var/lib/docker/volumes/<name>/_data -mindepth 1 -print -quit` returns nothing), push a `failed` "Compose up <dir>" step naming the volume ("its database volume <name> did not migrate — starting would run against an empty database; copy it from the old server, then bring the stack up") and `continue` — do NOT start the stack. To list a compose project's volumes + which service/image uses them, use `${composeCmd} ${ce.fileArg}${ce.args}config --format json` (parse `.volumes` and `.services[].volumes`) run on the target, or `docker compose ... config --volumes`. Be conservative: only HARD-refuse for stateful DB engines; for a non-DB empty volume, emit a WARNING step but still start (mirror the standalone path's warn-vs-refuse split).

## FIX F6 — union the volume copy list with the LIVE inspect (a volume on a not-running-at-scan container is missed → feeds F2/F3 empties)
The volume COPY loop iterates `plan.dockerVolumes` (from the stored wizard scan). The live inspect already captures named-volume mounts per container (`c.mounts` kind "volume", `{{.Name}}`). Union the copy set with the live-inspected named volumes from `srcContainers` (dedupe, validate names with the existing VOLNAME_RE) so a volume the wizard scan missed still gets copied. Keep the existing copy mechanics.

## FIX A1 — guard DB import from CLOBBERING a same-named database already on the target (opt-in to overwrite)
`mysqldump --databases` / `pg_dumpall` emit CREATE DATABASE + DROP TABLE, so importing onto a target that ALREADY holds a DB of that name destroys its data. Add a new flag `const OVERWRITE_TARGET_DATA = process.env.MIGRATE_OVERWRITE_TARGET_DATA === "1";` near the other flags. Before importing a dumped DB, check whether a non-empty DB of that name already exists on the target (for MySQL: `mysql -N -e "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='<db>'"`; for Postgres: check the DB exists and has user tables). If it exists AND `OVERWRITE_TARGET_DATA` is false → SKIP the import and push a `failed`/`copied` step naming the collision ("a database named <db> already exists on this server with data; not overwriting it — set MIGRATE_OVERWRITE_TARGET_DATA=1 to replace it, or migrate to a fresh server"). If the flag is true → proceed (log that it's overwriting). If the target DB doesn't exist / is empty → proceed as today. Apply to BOTH the mysql and postgres import paths. Keep the existing dump logic untouched; only gate the IMPORT.

## Constraints
- All new shell must be safe under the existing single-quoted `sh -c '…'` style; validate names before interpolating (reuse VOLNAME_RE / existing validators).
- Never make a migration LESS safe: when unsure, refuse-and-name rather than proceed. Preserve every existing honest gate.
- Keep edits surgical and within these regions. Finish only when tsc is clean and the consolidate test passes. Report the flag name, each fix's final line numbers, and how you resolved the compose project name for F2.
